title: Flaming Lips Jump to Third Man Records For First New LP in Six Years, ‘The Teardrop Throbs’
summary: The first single from the album due out on Jan. 22 is the Pink Floyd-indebted slow-burn "God Will Control the Werewolves."
body: After nearly four decades on Warner Records, the Flaming Lips are going indie again. The long-running psychedelic rock warriors lead by sole remaining original member singer Wayne Coyne announced their debut album for Jack White’s Third Man Records on Monday (Oct. 26). The album, The Teardrop Throbs , is due out on Jan. 22. The Lips’ 17th studio album overall and first LP of new material in six years was produced by the band along with Taylor Johnson, frequent collaborator Dave Fridmann and longtime manager Scott Booker, with additional production by Jon and Mike Fridmann. Ebullient singer Coyne, 65, elaborated on the LP’s origins in a lengthy essay in which he waxed rhapsodic about his bottomless love for his two young sons, Bloom Bobby, 7 and Rex Roses, 4, writing, “it occurred to me that there will never be anything in my life as important as my two little boys … to have arrived at the greatest of the greatest purposes in life … yes .. I am here.” He also gave the cute backstory for the collection’s first single, the Pink Floyd-indebted saucerful of trippy secrets, “God Will Control the Werewolves.” The floaty ballad o…

title: OnePlus’ Android 17 update is rolling out to older flagships
summary: Four more OnePlus phones join the Android 17 rollout.
body: TL;DR OnePlus is expanding its stable Android 17 rollout to the OnePlus 13, 13R, 13s, and 15R. The update introduces ColorOS 17, replacing OxygenOS with a refreshed interface, performance improvements, and new AI features. India gets the updates first, but the OnePlus 13, 13R, and 15R could get them in the US next. Android 17 is no longer just a treat for OnePlus’ newest devices. After the OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4 got the ball rolling , the update is now reaching more phones, including last year’s OnePlus 13 series. The rollout has started in India, bringing US owners one step closer to their turn. OnePlus has confirmed stable ColorOS 17 updates for the OnePlus 13, 13R, 13s, and 15R through separate posts on its community forums. That means the Android 17 rollout is already expanding beyond the first two devices, which received their updates ahead of the previously announced October 29 release date.

title: Android handhelds just got a massive multitasking upgrade with this launcher
summary: Cocoon 3.1 beta lets players quickly freeze and switch between active games.
body: TL;DR Cocoon 3.1 beta introduces Enhanced Device Access, allowing users to suspend, resume, and switch between games directly from the launcher grid. The update adds performance optimizations for lower-spec handhelds, a drag-and-resize grid editor, exact battery percentage counters, and dual-screen display swapping. The Cocoon 3.1 beta release is available to sideload via GitHub and includes a built-in auto-updater for future versions. Dedicated Android emulation frontends have made massive strides recently, with apps like ES-DE , Socket , and Blip elevating the Android handheld experience. Cocoon, a frontend tailored heavily for modern handhelds like the AYN Thor , has now picked up its 3.1 beta update. The highlight addition for this release is a new fast game-switching feature that lets users suspend, resume, and bounce between games seamlessly right from the home launcher. As detailed in the Cocoon 3.1 release notes and highlighted on Reddit , the feature is powered by a new “Enhanced Device Access” mode. With Cocoon 3.1 beta installed, pressing the Home button in a game now suspends the title on the launcher grid, leaving an active snapshot of where you left off. From there, …

title: I tested the Galaxy S26 Ultra and OPPO Find X10 Pro Max cameras — it’s no contest
summary: Are three 200MP cameras better than one? OPPO wants you to think so, so we found out.
body: How many 200-megapixel cameras do you need? Samsung thinks one is plenty, so it used it for the main camera on the back of the Galaxy S26 Ultra . OPPO thinks this is a bit feeble, and put three 200MP cameras on the back of the OPPO Find X10 Pro Max . Yes, three. The main, wide, and telephoto cameras all have 200 megapixels. What’s more, it has worked closely with Samsung itself developing one of them, and then with camera experts Hasselblad to tune the performance.

title: The iOS-ification of Android is ruining my favorite phones
summary: I love Android, but its obsession with copying Liquid Glass is starting to get on my nerves.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority There’s arguably never been a better time to be an Android fan. There’s a wide range of brands, each with something unique to offer; long-term software updates are now the norm, and high-end hardware even eclipses what the ever-popular iPhone has to offer. Whether you’re looking for a powerhouse gaming smartphone, one with the best battery life, the most cutting-edge AI tools, or the most versatile camera setup on the market, there’s an Android phone for you. I’ve recently had the pleasure of running the OPPO Find X10 Pro Max for a few weeks, a brilliant phone by virtually every metric you can throw at it. Multi-day battery life, silky smooth performance, a top-notch camera, and even some brilliant first-party software. OPPO’s unique aesthetic also ensures this isn’t a phone you’d easily confuse for a Galaxy or iPhone knock-off. It looks and feels like something very unique, a compliment you could pay quite a few Android brands these days, at least when looking at the back of the handsets.

title: The MOVA V70 Ultra Complete isn’t perfect, but it solves one big robot vacuum problem
summary: Reach out and clean something!
body: If you’re not using a robot vacuum yet, you do not know what you’re missing. I first started getting into the tech properly as a reviewer earlier this year, expecting disappointment at every turn, and I could not have been more wrong — these products have years of refinement under their belts, and are effortlessly capable of delivering a really impressive cleaning experience. But for as good as they are, that refinement has only begun to highlight some of the areas where there’s still clear room for improvement. Yet so often with autonomous devices, that’s exactly where things start going wrong — those problems are left for last for good reason.

title: I’m playing Super Mario Galaxy on my Android phone. Here’s how to get it on yours right now
summary: Let this one cook a bit longer.
body: Emulation isn’t new, and neither is running Nintendo games on smartphone hardware. Nintendo’s portable-first console experiences translate beautifully to smartphone hardware, making its platform a prime target for emulation. However, as good as emulation is, a native port always hits differently due to the performance improvements and reduced latency that it brings. Earlier this week, I came across a project dubbed Galaxy Android that brings Super Mario Galaxy, widely considered one of the greatest 3D platformers ever created, to Android as a native experience. Released as part of the OpenPort Labs project, the Android build makes copious use of AI to get it up and running, but it’s important to acknowledge the seven and a half years of effort by the Petari decompilation project to write the code by hand. With that in mind, the only real question was to see how well it performed.

title: Samsung Community is going dark for 3 days, and you might want to take preemptive action
summary: Here's what you need to know.
body: TL;DR Samsung Community will go offline for 72 hours starting October 30 as the company prepares a major platform overhaul. Some user data, including direct messages, saved drafts, bookmarks, and subscriptions, won’t survive the migration. Users should create backups. The revamped platform will introduce changes to direct messaging, accepted solutions, and post deletion rules when it returns on November 2. If you’re a Samsung Galaxy user, there’s a good chance you’ve tried out the tech giant’s Community platform. Samsung Community, which is available as a standalone website, is also integrated into the Samsung Members app. It is an official forum that lets Samsung users connect, ask questions, share tips, and find news and announcements. It’s a useful resource, and that’s precisely why you might want to take note of an upcoming disruption. The good news is that Samsung is giving the platform a “major overhaul.” The bad news is that the platform will soon be offline for 72 hours, and some of your data might not make it through the transition.

Users will be able to set trusted exclusion zones to silence separation alerts at specific places, such as home, either globally or per device. Upcoming controls will let users move notification and reverse-ringing settings between devices without unpairing and re-enrolling accessories. As Google gears up for the November 11 first sale of its long-awaited Pixel Tag , the company is actively laying the groundwork to ensure its tracking ecosystem is ready for it. Google has been working on Left-Behind reminders for the Find Hub ecosystem , and the feature made an appearance in the recent October Google Play Services Update changelog as well. We’ve now spotted more clues in Find Hub that indicate further progress on these key tracking accessory features, and they should put your mind at ease if you were planning to buy the Pixel Tag. title: Instagram is coming for YouTube’s crown with long-form videos
summary: YouTube has ruled long-form video practically unchallenged. Now Instagram wants a seat at the table.
body: TL;DR Instagram is testing Features, allowing select US creators to publish horizontal videos up to 90 minutes long. The new format connects short Reels to full-length videos, potentially positioning Instagram as a serious YouTube competitor. Instagram’s massive audience gives it an advantage, but matching YouTube’s creator monetization remains a challenge. That hilarious podcast clip in your Reels feed has one awkward ending: the rest is on YouTube . Instagram wants to rewrite that ending, and Google’s video giant might finally have a rival with the audience to make it interesting. Instagram is testing Features, a format for horizontal videos up to 90 minutes long. Following an earlier trial in Brazil, select US creators can now experiment with full-length podcasts, comedy specials, and other long-form content. Reels can link directly to the full videos, and Instagram also plans to recommend them through Explore. Eventually, the experience should reach its growing TV app .

title: Acer’s Intel Arc-powered Steam Deck rival finally gets a price and release date
summary: Acer's new gaming beast is almost ready to leave its cage.
body: TL;DR Acer’s Predator Atlas 8 gaming handheld launches November 1, exclusively at Best Buy, for $1,300. The handheld packs Intel’s Arc G3 Extreme processor, an 8-inch 120Hz VRR display, an 80Wh battery, and Windows 11. Acer says the first round of pre-orders sold out last week, even before the handheld hit shelves. Gaming handhelds have become quite capable in recent years. Devices like the Steam Deck and ASUS ROG Ally let you take your favorite PC games almost anywhere. Now, Acer wants a piece of that action, too, but its latest handheld comes with a price tag that might make you think twice. First unveiled at Computex 2026, the Acer Predator Atlas 8 goes on sale November 1, exclusively at Best Buy . And while we’ve known about the handheld for a while, Acer has now revealed one important detail: it’ll cost $1,300. That’s a lot of money for a portable gaming device, but it hasn’t scared everyone away. According to Acer, the first round of pre-orders sold out last week. If you missed out, online orders will reopen on November 1, when the handheld also arrives in stores.

title: The best PS2 emulator on Android can now make performance tweaks for you
summary: ARMSX2 on Android can automatically change settings, one at a time, to find the best performance.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR ARMSX2 has marked its one-year anniversary with the v2.9 update. The PS2 emulator can now automatically tweak your game’s settings to improve performance. It also runs faster on the Retroid Pocket Duo, while two other additions also deliver better performance. ARMSX2 is arguably the best PS2 emulator on Android , and that’s largely due to a steady stream of updates. It turns out that the project is celebrating its one-year anniversary, and the team has released a significant update to mark the occasion. ARMSX2 v2.9 has been released on GitHub and the Play Store , and brings some noteworthy features and improvements. Perhaps the standout feature is Automatic Performance Tuning, as the emulator can now make several changes in the background to improve speeds.

title: Disturbed to Play ‘The Sickness’ in Full on Australia and New Zealand Tour
summary: The band will perform its 2000 debut start to finish, followed by a greatest-hits set, across seven arena dates in April and May 2027.
body: Disturbed are heading back to Australia and New Zealand in 2027 for their first headline tour of the region in more than a decade. The seven-date arena run will begin April 22 at Auckland’s Spark Arena before heading to Christchurch, Brisbane, Sydney, Adelaide and Melbourne, wrapping May 9 at Perth’s RAC Arena. Each night will feature two Disturbed sets. The first will see the band perform their 2000 debut album, The Sickness , in full, while the second will draw from more than two decades of hits. The Australia and New Zealand dates follow the band’s The Sickness 25th-anniversary tour across North America, the U.K. and Europe, where Disturbed have been revisiting the album that launched their career. Released in March 2000, The Sickness peaked at No. 29 on the Billboard 200 and became one of the defining hard-rock releases of the early 2000s. The album has since been certified five-times platinum by the RIAA. Its best-known track, “Down With the Sickness,” remains one of Disturbed’s signature songs, while the band later found another major crossover moment with their 2015 cover of Simon & Garfunkel’s “The Sound of Silence.” That track became Disturbed’s highest-charting entry…

title: This emulator just cut off support to Anbernic’s upcoming Nintendo 3DS clone
summary: Anbernic's RG DDS gets some bad news before launch.
body: Credit: YouTube TL;DR Anbernic is in trouble for featuring an “unofficial piracy-focused” fork of the 3DS emulator Azahar in its promotional material for the RG DDS. The Azahar team has announced it will no longer support devices made by Anbernic. The team warns that it will not investigate or resolve issues or bugs related to devices from this manufacturer. There’s a fair amount of excitement for the release of the Anbernic RG DDS. Putting a bit of a damper on the upcoming launch, a pricing leak suggests the Nintendo 3DS clone could cost more than expected. In another blow to whatever level of anticipation you may have, the team behind Azahar is pulling its support. Anbernic has found itself in a bit of hot water after publishing its most recent promotional video for the handheld. In the video, the company features its own forked version of Azahar (a 3DS emulator), which it calls “Azahar Plus.” This video has not escaped the attention of the Azahar team.

title: Apple finally breaks its silence on iPhone Duo’s cracked screens
summary: Apple's first foldable is getting a crash course in first-generation problems.
body: TL;DR Apple has acknowledged an issue affecting the iPhone Duo’s inner display following reports of screens cracking near the hinge. The admission follows CEO John Ternus’s recent claim that early Android foldables were “kind of cheap and crappy.” Apple says only a small number of units are affected and advises owners experiencing problems to contact AppleCare for a replacement. Apple may have taken its sweet time joining the foldable party , but it hasn’t escaped the growing pains that greeted some of its Android rivals years ago. Just days after the $1,999 iPhone Duo went on sale, Apple has officially acknowledged reports of inner displays cracking near the hinge. It’s an uncomfortable development for a company that waited years to get foldables right, especially after its CEO recently took a swipe at earlier attempts.

title: Google is building a home for everything you’ve asked Gemini to remember
summary: Soon, you might not need to explicitly ask Gemini what it remembers.
body: TL;DR Google is working on a new “Remembered items” section within Gemini’s Personal Intelligence settings. The feature will let users view and manage text and images they’ve explicitly asked Gemini to remember. The interface is accessible with flags enabled, but it isn’t fully functional yet. Gemini is getting increasingly good at offering personalized information , and its memory plays a huge part in making that possible. The AI tool learns your preferences over time, but you also have the option to explicitly ask it to remember specific things for future reference. We’ve previously spotted Google working on making the process of asking Gemini to remember things easier, and it looks like the tech giant is now focusing on what happens afterward. As of right now, the easiest way to check everything you’ve explicitly asked Gemini to remember is to ask the AI assistant directly. That could soon change.

title: Survey shows most readers stand by Android, but a good number are iOS-curious
summary: Pixel disappointments play a part for those considering switching.
body: Switching from an iPhone to an Android or vice versa is not the headache it once was. That goes for both the learning curves, or lack thereof, between the platforms, and the tools that now exist that easily port over all of your information. But that doesn’t mean that old rivalries aren’t still at play. Recently, Android Authority’s Harish Jonnalagadda spent three weeks with the iPhone 18 Pro Max and came away with a fairly positive opinion. We put a poll for you, our readers, in the story asking if you would consider switching to iOS at some point, and the reaction was strong. It shouldn’t be much of a surprise that the majority of people who are on an Android-focused site want only Android devices in their pockets. Out of the 1,265 respondents, 52.8% declared themselves “Android for life.”

title: Gemini could soon make it easier to purge old, unwanted conversations
summary: Managing Gemini chat history could get simpler with a new multi-select tool.
body: TL;DR Gemini users can reference a past list of their conversations with the AI. Right now you can select individual conversations and choose to share, pin or delete. Gemini may soon allow you to select multiple conversations at once, for easy bulk deletion. At this point, it’s probably fair to say that a growing number of us have a bit of a love–hate relationship when it comes to many things AI. Sure, we appreciate its ability to help summarize reams of material, generate fantastical imagery, and even help us code apps , but all that power is also exactly why it’s worth approaching with a modicum of caution. One of the many ways we manage that is by controlling our AI history , limiting its ability to reference past interactions. And now it looks like Gemini is working on a new feature up that alley. title: I thought I’d love the $180 Fitbit Edge. 7 days later, I’m just disappointed.
summary: Not the wearable I was hoping for.
body: Over the last few months, my priorities in wearables have changed. I’ve realized I don’t care about having Gemini on my wrist, multiple ways to reply to notifications, or even a robust app ecosystem. I simply want a wearable that’s comfortable on my wrist, lasts multiple days on a single charge, and offers a health/fitness tracking suite I enjoy using. As such, I was really looking forward to the Fitbit Edge. Taking the week-long battery life of the excellent Fitbit Air and giving it a proper touchscreen — all while retaining a small and lightweight design — sounded like the perfect combination. And in some ways, it is.

title: Apple just eliminated Android’s biggest advantages in compact tablets with the new iPad mini
summary: By adopting an OLED display, A20 Pro SoC, and IP67 durability, Apple leaves rival mini slates with virtually no counter.
body: TL;DR The newly redesigned iPad mini eliminates traditional Android advantages by adding an 8.5-inch OLED display and a durable IP67 dust- and water-resistant rating in a 5.4mm frame. Powered by the 2nm A20 Pro chip alongside custom N1 wireless and C2 5G silicon, it outperforms budget-tier Android slates while retaining Apple Pencil Pro support. A $200 price hike to $699 leaves room for potential Android challengers, but weak market interest means Apple will likely maintain its grip on the segment. Apple has officially unveiled the redesigned iPad mini, handing its smallest slate an overdue top-to-bottom transformation highlighted by a shift to OLED, a new SoC, and a thinner chassis. The announcement is the first in Apple’s late-October iPad and Mac showcase but follows the HomeView reveal earlier in the month, positioning the petite tablet less as a casual media viewer and more like a pocketable iPad Air.

summary: Chromebooks have the handy Welcome Recap feature, and it looks like this is coming to Googlebook OS.

title: The best original Xbox emulator on Android just got a huge performance upgrade
summary: It might even run on your potato of a device.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR The developer behind the HakuX emulator for Android has released v1.0.0 and v1.1.0 of the app. These new versions bring major performance upgrades, allowing us to run original Xbox games on budget-tier Android hardware. These updates also bring improved support for non-Snapdragon processors. There was a dearth of original Xbox emulators for Android , but that started to change earlier this year. We first saw the admittedly vibecoded X1 Box app in March, based on the Xemu emulator for PC, but this was quickly followed by a forked Android app called HakuX. Thankfully, there’s some great news if you want better original Xbox emulation on Android. The developer behind HakuX has released v1.0.0 of the emulator on GitHub , bringing some major upgrades. For starters, the emulator is no longer based on Xemu’s CPU tech. More specifically, the app now uses the FEX tool to translate x86 CPU instructions to Arm. The developer also claims that the Xbox kernel is reimplemented natively.

title: The ASUS ROG Xbox Ally X20 is the best (and priciest) Ally yet
summary: Oh no, I think I want one.
body: Last year, ASUS and Microsoft teamed up to release the ROG Xbox Ally and ROG Xbox Ally X. The handheld gaming PCs were Microsoft’s first real push into the space, debuting a new full-screen Xbox interface to help bridge the gap between PC and console-style gaming experiences. The higher-end Xbox Ally X was particularly well received, with multiple outlets crowning it the best Windows-powered gaming handheld of the year. Now, Xbox and ASUS are back with an even higher-end Xbox Ally handheld: the ASUS ROG Xbox Ally X20 . The X20 features the same AMD Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme processor and 24 GB of LPDDR5X memory as last year’s Xbox Ally X, along with a great new OLED display, a sleek transparent plastic shell, updated controls, and more. After gaming on the thing for a couple of weeks, I’m really impressed — but Windows is an iffy handheld OS, and the X20’s $1,300 price tag may be a tough sell for everyone but the perfect target audience.

title: Snapseed is prepping a major upgrade for long exposure photography
summary: A future update could let you choose from multiple long exposure modes before capturing a photo.
body: TL;DR The Snapseed app is working on a major camera interface upgrade that could add long exposure capture modes. Some of the options we’ve uncovered include Light trails, Silky water, Night, Live Photo, and more. These modes would let Snapseed users adjust exposure for various environments before capturing an image through its camera interface. The Snapseed app currently includes a Pro camera interface that lets you manually adjust ISO, shutter speed, and focus before you capture a photo. These are key controls for photographers who want to get more out of their images in different environments. We can now report on a potential addition to Snapseed that could further expand its feature set. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. The mockery comes as Apple’s first foldable faces early reports of cracked screens and durability concerns. title: OnePlus reveals clip-style earbuds that you can wear in either ear
summary: The new OnePlus Buds Clip can automatically detect which ear you're wearing either earbud in.
body: TL;DR OnePlus has revealed the OnePlus Buds Clip, its first open-ear wireless earbuds featuring an adaptive nickel-titanium C-bridge and interchangeable left/right ear detection. The earbuds feature Dynaudio-tuned dual drivers (11mm woofer and 9mm tweeter), LHDC 5.0 Hi-Res support, and dipole sound-field technology to minimize audio leakage. Offering up to 40 hours of total battery life, Bluetooth 6.1, and an IP55 rating, the OnePlus Buds Clip are listed globally in three colors, though pricing and availability are yet to be announced. OnePlus has exited the US and EU markets, but it still operates in some global regions. OnePlus has now officially entered the open-ear audio space with the reveal of the OnePlus Buds Clip, joining the growing segment of clip-style true wireless earphones that are designed for all-day awareness and comfort, and taking direct aim at rivals such as the Bose Ultra Open (2nd Gen) Earbuds and the Sony LinkBuds Clip . OnePlus has already listed the OnePlus Buds Clip on its global website , indicating that the product is intended for a wider release beyond its home market of China.

title: Samsung’s first clip-on Galaxy Buds launch tomorrow, and there’s good news for global buyers
summary: Samsung's new Buds are all ears, and the world might be next.
body: TL;DR Samsung’s first clip-on earbuds, the Galaxy Buds On, go on sale in South Korea on October 27 for around $226. The earbuds feature an open-ear design, TwinBoost speakers, and Galaxy AI features, including head gestures and voice memos. European retail listings hint at an upcoming global launch, with prices ranging from $216 to $241 in Switzerland. Samsung has made wireless earbuds for years, but its latest pair is unlike anything we’ve seen from the company. Earlier this month, Samsung quietly introduced the Galaxy Buds On , its first clip-on earbuds that let you listen to music without blocking your ears. They go on sale tomorrow, October 27, in South Korea. And there’s some good news for those waiting to get their hands on them outside Samsung’s home market. If you missed our earlier coverage , the Galaxy Buds On feature an open-ear design that lets you enjoy music without losing touch with your surroundings. So, whether you’re listening to your favorite podcast on a morning walk while keeping an ear out for traffic, or enjoying music at work without missing someone calling your name, there’s plenty to appreciate about this approach.

title: Google TV Streamer is now two years old: is it still worth getting?
summary: Google's streaming box has had two years to make its case, but is it still the best Android TV player?
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority The Google TV Streamer was a big swing when it arrived in 2024, marking the end of the company’s Chromecast legacy. It not only dropped the Chromecast name, but also delivered a much more premium experience. I’ve personally owned Google’s latest streamer for all but the first six months of the product’s lifecycle, and while it’s not perfect, I’ve mostly enjoyed the experience. Of course, two years is a long time in the tech world. While there are rumors that a new model could eventually surface in the not-too-distant future, the bigger question isn’t just how well the hardware holds up. Is the Google TV Streamer line actually an improvement over the company’s older strategy? Honestly, I’m still not fully certain.

title: One UI 9 could have caught up to Google, but Samsung is still missing one thing
summary: Samsung needs to do more to make One UI's selling point more robust.
body: I remember the pain of firing up Samsung’s TouchWiz on my Galaxy phones. The software was laggy, unintuitive, and rarely updated. Quarterly security patches on flagship phones would be unacceptable in 2026, but that was the norm for Samsung devices. That all changed with the introduction of One UI. Samsung flipped the script and became known for reliable software with timely updates. One UI 9 running Android 17 is undoubtedly another solid software update. It’s been a smooth experience so far on my Galaxy S26 Plus , and Samsung’s been spot-on with patches. But while the company has made great strides in software, its pitch for Galaxy AI still leaves me unconvinced. Features like Now Brief and Now Nudge haven’t lived up to their potential, and Google’s Pixel software does a better job of making AI feel like a natural part of the experience.

title: YouTube streams may look better and buffer less as soon as early 2027
summary: AV2 is coming to YouTube in the not too distant future.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR YouTube has announced that it plans to roll out AV2 to the platform in early 2027. The AV2 codec will initially launch for the web version of YouTube. The company also hints at benefits for multi-view experiences. Earlier this year, the Alliance for Open Media released the definitive specs for the AV2 codec , which is expected to be about 25% to 32% more efficient than AV1. That means you get higher-quality streaming for the same bitrate or comparable quality at a lower bitrate. The benefit is that the codec can reduce the amount of bandwidth you’re consuming. YouTube is expected to adopt AV2, and it could arrive sooner than you would expect. While partners like Netflix, Amazon, and Apple have been quiet on rollout plans, it appears that YouTube isn’t quite as shy. According to FlatpanelsHD , YouTube has revealed that it is looking to roll out the codec in early 2027. The plan is to initially launch AV2 for the web version of the platform.

title: 5 streaming boxes you should buy instead of the new Apple TV 4K
summary: You don't need to spend $299 to stream Netflix.
body: Soaring memory and chip prices have been having an adverse effect on hardware prices for a few months. Apple already raised its streaming box’s prices some time ago, but the long-anticipated Apple TV 4K 2026 recently launched with an even higher, eye-watering price tag of $299, bringing it right on par with the Nvidia Shield TV Pro after its recent hike. For comparison, the previous Apple TV 4K used to start at a much more palatable $129. Not too long ago, there were rumors that Apple might release an even cheaper variant next — but it went the opposite way. $300 is way too much money to watch Netflix while you scroll on your phone — you can get a full-blown TV for that kind of price these days. If you don’t mind stepping outside Apple’s walled garden, you can easily snag a much better deal where you not only get premium hardware and all the associated perks, but also save tons of cash upfront.
